results.title: Coefficients of a product with a homogeneous linear polynomial

results.title: Coefficient list after multiplication by a linear polynomial

results.title: Length of the coefficient list after a linear multiplication

results.title: Coefficient recurrence for multiplication by a linear polynomial
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Coefficient-list multiplication agrees with polynomial multiplication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Interpreting the dense output as a little-endian polynomial is left multiplication by the linear polynomial `C r + X * C c`.

results.title: Expansion of a product of affine linear polynomials

results.title: Coefficients of a product of affine linear polynomials

results.title: Degree bound for a product of affine linear polynomials

results.title: Binomial bound on coefficients of a product of affine polynomials

results.title: Dyadic rationals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real number $x$ is dyadic when $x = a / 2^n$ for some integer $a$ and some natural number $n$, that is, when $x$ lies in $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$.

results.title: Golden integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\tau = (1 + \sqrt{5})/2$ be the golden ratio. A real number $x$ is a golden integer when $x = a + b\tau$ for some integers $a$ and $b$. Since $\tau^2 = \tau + 1$, these are exactly the elements of $\mathbb{Z}[\tau]$.

results.title: Piecewise-linear maps with prescribed breakpoints and slopes
results.caption: Definition

A permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{R}$ is piecewise linear with breakpoints in $B$ and slopes in $S$ when $f(x) = x$ for every $x \notin [0, 1]$, and there are a natural number $n$ and points $0 = t_0 < t_1 < \dots < t_{n+1} = 1$, all in $B$, such that for each $i \le n$ there is $s \in S$ with $f(x) = f(t_i) + s (x - t_i)$ for all $x \in [t_i, t_{i+1}]$.

part.title: Kaluza's theorem on reciprocal power series

path: Kaluza's theorem on reciprocal power series

results.title: Positive log-convex coefficients
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real formal power series $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ has positive log-convex coefficients if $a_n > 0$ for every natural number $n$ and $a_{n+1}^2 \le a_n a_{n+2}$ for every natural number $n$. This is the hypothesis of Kaluza's bounds for the coefficients of the reciprocal series.

results.title: Coefficients of a positive log-convex series are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a real formal power series $f$ has positive log-convex coefficients, then the coefficient of $X^n$ in $f$ is strictly positive for every natural number $n$.

results.title: Log-convexity of the coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a real formal power series $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ has positive log-convex coefficients, then $a_{n+1}^2 \le a_n a_{n+2}$ for every natural number $n$.

results.title: Kaluza's bounds for the coefficients of a reciprocal power series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ be a real formal power series with positive log-convex coefficients, and let $f^{-1} = \sum_n b_n X^n$ be its reciprocal in the ring of formal power series. Then $b_0 = a_0^{-1}$, $b_0 > 0$, and $-a_n / a_0^2 \le b_n \le 0$ for every $n \ge 1$.

children.title: Separable extensions over separably closed fields

results.title: Field generated by the image of a finite algebra is finite-dimensional
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `S` is finite over `R` and `χ' : S →+* K` sends `R` into the image of `E` in `K`, then the field generated over `E` by the range of `χ'` is finite-dimensional over `E`.

results.title: Finite separable extensions are quotients by separable irreducible polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L/K$ be a finite field extension. Then $L/K$ is separable if and only if there is a monic, irreducible, separable polynomial $f \in K[X]$ such that $L$ is isomorphic as a $K$-algebra to $K[X]/(f)$.

results.title: Purely inseparable extensions of prime degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p$, and let $L/K$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension of degree $[L : K] = p$. Then there are $\alpha \in L$ and $a \in K$ such that the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K$ is $X^p - a$, $a$ is not a $p$-th power in $K$ (that is, $b^p \neq a$ for every $b \in K$), and $L = K(\alpha)$.

results.title: Tsen's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $k(X)$ the field of rational functions over $k$. For all natural numbers $n$ and $d$ with $0 < d < n$, every homogeneous polynomial $f$ of degree $d$ in $n$ variables over $k(X)$ has a nontrivial zero: there is $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n) \in k(X)^n$ with $x_i \neq 0$ for some $i$ and $f(x) = 0$. In other words, $k(X)$ is a $C_1$ field.

results.title: Equilateral triangle with given side
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $s$, a finite set $T$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ is an equilateral triangle of side $s$ when $T$ has exactly three elements and any two distinct points of $T$ are at distance $s$.

results.title: Unit equilateral triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $T$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a unit equilateral triangle when it is an equilateral triangle of side $1$: $T$ has exactly three elements and any two distinct points of $T$ are at distance $1$.

results.title: Equilateral triangle of any size
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $T$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ is an equilateral triangle of any size when there is a real number $s > 0$ such that $T$ is an equilateral triangle of side $s$: $T$ has exactly three elements and any two distinct points of $T$ are at distance $s$.

When such sets exist this is the largest such number; when none exist (only for $d = 0$ and $n \ge 2$) it is $0$.

results.title: Unit sphere packing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is the centre set of a unit sphere packing if the open balls of radius $1$ centred at any two distinct points of $X$ are disjoint.

results.title: Optimal sphere packing density

results.title: Measurable partition modulo null sets
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $M$. A finite family $P$ of subsets of $M$ is a measurable partition of $M$ modulo $\mu$-null sets when every member of $P$ is measurable, the complement of the union of the members of $P$ has $\mu$-measure $0$, and any two distinct members $A \ne B$ of $P$ satisfy $\mu(A \cap B) = 0$.

Here $\mu(A)$ is taken as a real number, so a set of infinite measure contributes $0$.

results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function. For every $m \in K$ and every integer $k$, the integer $\operatorname{rne}(m)$ obtained by rounding $m$ to the nearest integer, ties to even, satisfies $|\operatorname{rne}(m) - m| \le |k - m|$: no integer is closer to $m$ than $\operatorname{rne}(m)$.

results.title: Rounding to the nearest integer is within one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function. For every $m \in K$, the integer $\operatorname{rne}(m)$ obtained by rounding $m$ to the nearest integer, ties to even, satisfies $|\operatorname{rne}(m) - m| \le 1/2$.

results.title: Ties to even for the nearest integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $m \in K$, and let $\operatorname{rne}(m)$ be the integer obtained by rounding $m$ to the nearest integer, ties to even. If $|\operatorname{rne}(m) - m| = 1/2$, that is, $m$ is halfway between two consecutive integers, then $\operatorname{rne}(m)$ is even.

results.title: Rounding to nearest preserves integer upper bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $m \in K$ and let $k$ be an integer. If $m \le k$, then $\operatorname{rne}(m) \le k$, where $\operatorname{rne}(m)$ is $m$ rounded to the nearest integer with ties to even.

results.title: Rounding to nearest preserves integer lower bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $m \in K$ and let $k$ be an integer. If $k \le m$, then $k \le \operatorname{rne}(m)$, where $\operatorname{rne}(m)$ is $m$ rounded to the nearest integer with ties to even.

results.title: Binary floating-point numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$, an element $x$ of a linearly ordered field with a floor function is a binary floating-point number with a $p$-bit significand and unbounded exponent when $x = m \cdot 2^e$ for some integers $m$ and $e$ with $|m| < 2^p$.

results.title: Floating-point numbers of a bounded format
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$ and integers $q_{\min}$ and $q_{\max}$, an element $x$ of a linearly ordered field with a floor function is a number of the binary format with $p$-bit significands and last-place exponents in $[q_{\min}, q_{\max}]$ when $x = m \cdot 2^e$ for some integers $m$ and $e$ with $|m| < 2^p$ and $q_{\min} \le e \le q_{\max}$. These are zero, the subnormal numbers and the normal numbers of the format.

results.title: Exponent of the last place
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$ (the significand length) and $x$ in a linearly ordered field $K$ with a floor function, the exponent of the last place of $x$ is the integer $\lfloor \log_2 |x| \rfloor - (p - 1)$. Here $\lfloor \log_2 |x| \rfloor$ is the integer logarithm: the largest integer $n$ with $2^n \le |x|$ when $x \ne 0$, and $0$ when $x = 0$.

results.title: Round to nearest, ties to even
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$ and an element $x$ of a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $e$ be the exponent of the last place of $x$ at precision $p$, and let $\operatorname{rne}$ round to the nearest integer with ties to the even one. The rounding of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, is $\mathrm{fl}_p(x) = \operatorname{rne}(x / 2^e) \cdot 2^e$: scale $x$ so that its last place is the units digit, round to…

results.title: Bounds on the scaled significand
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $p \ge 1$ be a natural number and let $x \in K$ be nonzero. Let $e = \lfloor \log_2 |x| \rfloor - (p - 1)$ be the exponent of the last place of $x$ for $p$-bit significands. Then $2^{p-1} \le |x / 2^e|$ and $|x / 2^e| < 2^p$.

results.title: The rounding error at the scale of the last place
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ be an element of a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $p$ be a natural number, and let $e$ be the exponent of the last place of $x$ at precision $p$. Writing $\operatorname{rne}$ for rounding to the nearest integer with ties to even, the rounding $\mathrm{fl}_p(x)$ of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, at precision $p$ has the error…

results.title: The relative error bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function and let $p$ be a natural number. For every $x \in K$, the rounding $\mathrm{fl}(x)$ of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, with $p$-bit significands satisfies $|\mathrm{fl}(x) - x| \le u\,|x|$, where $u = 2^{-p}$ is the unit roundoff.

results.title: Round to nearest for floating-point numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function and let $p \ge 1$. For every $x \in K$ and every binary floating-point number $f \in K$ with a $p$-bit significand (and unbounded exponent), the rounding $\mathrm{fl}(x)$ of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, with $p$-bit significands satisfies $|\mathrm{fl}(x) - x| \le |f - x|$: no floating-point number is closer to $x$ than $\mathrm{fl}(x)$.

results.title: Floating-point numbers round to themselves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \ge 1$ and let $x$ be an element of a linearly ordered field with a floor function. If $x$ is a binary floating-point number with a $p$-bit significand, that is, $x = m \cdot 2^e$ for some integers $m$ and $e$ with $|m| < 2^p$, then rounding $x$ to nearest, ties to even, at precision $p$ returns $x$: $\mathrm{fl}_p(x) = x$.

results.title: Ties to even for floating-point rounding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $p$ be a natural number, let $x \in K$, and let $e$ be the exponent of the last place of $x$, which is $\lfloor \log_2 |x| \rfloor - (p - 1)$ for $x \ne 0$. If the rounding $\mathrm{fl}(x)$ of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, with $p$-bit significands satisfies $|\mathrm{fl}(x) - x| = 2^e / 2$, then the integer $\operatorname{rne}(x / 2^e)$, the…

results.title: Bound on the rounded significand
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $p \ge 1$, let $x \in K$ be nonzero, and let $e = \lfloor \log_2 |x| \rfloor - (p - 1)$ be the exponent of the last place of $x$. Then $|\operatorname{rne}(x / 2^e)| \le 2^p$, where $\operatorname{rne}$ rounds to the nearest integer, ties to even.

results.title: Rounding gives a floating-point number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \ge 1$. For every element $x$ of a linearly ordered field with a floor function, the rounding $\mathrm{fl}_p(x)$ of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, is a binary floating-point number with a $p$-bit significand: $\mathrm{fl}_p(x) = m \cdot 2^e$ for some integers $m$ and $e$ with $|m| < 2^p$.

results.title: In the normal range, rounding stays in the format
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \ge 1$, let $q_{\min}$ and $q_{\max}$ be integers, and let $x$ be an element of a linearly ordered field with a floor function. If $2^{q_{\min} + p - 1} \le |x|$ ($x$ is at least the smallest normal number) and $|x| \le (2^p - 1) \cdot 2^{q_{\max}}$ ($x$ is at most the largest finite number), then the rounding $\mathrm{fl}_p(x)$ of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, is a number of the binary format with $p$-bit…

results.title: Round to nearest in a bounded format
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function, let $p \ge 1$, and let $q_{\min}$ and $q_{\max}$ be integers. For every $x \in K$ and every number $f$ of the binary format with $p$-bit significands and last-place exponents in $[q_{\min}, q_{\max}]$, the rounding $\mathrm{fl}(x)$ of $x$ to nearest, ties to even, with $p$-bit significands satisfies $|\mathrm{fl}(x) - x| \le |f - x|$.

results.title: The difference of floating-point numbers within a factor of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field with a floor function and let $p$ be a natural number. Let $x, y \in K$ and let $m_x, m_y, e_x, e_y$ be integers with $|m_x| < 2^p$, $|m_y| < 2^p$, $x = m_x 2^{e_x}$ and $y = m_y 2^{e_y}$. If $y / 2 \le x \le 2y$, then there is an integer $k$ with $|k| < 2^p$ and $x - y = k \cdot 2^{\min(e_x, e_y)}$.

results.title: Sterbenz's lemma
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number and let $x$ and $y$ be binary floating-point numbers with $p$-bit significands (and unbounded exponent) in a linearly ordered field with a floor function. If $y / 2 \le x \le 2y$, then $x - y$ is also a binary floating-point number with a $p$-bit significand.

results.title: Sterbenz's lemma in a bounded format
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number, let $q_{\min}$ and $q_{\max}$ be integers, and let $x$ and $y$ be numbers of the binary format with $p$-bit significands whose last place has exponent in $[q_{\min}, q_{\max}]$ (subnormal numbers included), in a linearly ordered field with a floor function. If $y / 2 \le x \le 2y$, then $x - y$ is also a number of this format.

results.title: Floating-point subtraction is exact under Sterbenz's condition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \ge 1$ and let $x$ and $y$ be binary floating-point numbers with $p$-bit significands in a linearly ordered field with a floor function. If $y / 2 \le x \le 2y$, then rounding $x - y$ to nearest, ties to even, at precision $p$ returns it exactly: $\mathrm{fl}_p(x - y) = x - y$.

results.title: Identity-by-descent recursion in Wright's island model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One generation of Wright's island-model identity-by-descent recursion for a deme of `M` gene copies (`M = 2N` for `N` diploids) receiving a fraction `m` of migrants from an infinite pool: `F' = (1 - m) ^ 2 * (1 / M + (1 - 1 / M) * F)`. Biologically meaningful for `M ≥ 2` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`; `M = 1` is an algebraic extension (no pair of distinct copies exists), and at `M = 0` Lean's `1 / 0 = 0` gives a junk value.

results.title: Equilibrium $F_{ST}$ of Wright's island model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The equilibrium identity-by-descent probability (Wright's `F_ST`) of the island model: `F* = (1 - m) ^ 2 / (M - (M - 1) (1 - m) ^ 2)`. Biologically meaningful for `M ≥ 2` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`; the denominator is positive already for `M ≥ 1` (`islandEquilibrium_denom_pos`), where `M = 1` is an algebraic extension.

results.title: Island-model contraction factor lies in (0, 1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `M ≥ 1` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`, the per-generation contraction factor `(1 - m) ^ 2 (1 - 1 / M)` lies in `[0, 1)`.

results.title: Positivity of the island-model equilibrium denominator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The denominator `M - (M - 1) (1 - m) ^ 2` of the equilibrium is positive (at least `1`) for `M ≥ 1` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`.

results.title: Island-model equilibrium is a fixed point of the recursion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `F*` is a fixed point of the island-model recursion.

results.title: Uniqueness of the island-model fixed point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `F*` is the only fixed point of the island-model recursion.

results.title: Geometric approach to equilibrium
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: After `t` generations, `F_t - F* = ((1 - m) ^ 2 (1 - 1 / M)) ^ t (F_0 - F*)`.

results.title: Convergence to equilibrium
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `M ≥ 1` and `0 ≤ m ≤ 1`, the island-model recursion converges to `F*` from every initial value `F₀`.

results.title: Island-model equilibrium lies in (0, 1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The equilibrium identity-by-descent probability lies in `[0, 1]`.

results.title: Island-model equilibrium is below one under migration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With migration (`0 < m ≤ 1`) the equilibrium identity-by-descent probability lies in `[0, 1)`.

results.title: Complete identity by descent in isolated demes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Isolated demes (`m = 0`): the equilibrium is complete identity by descent, `F* = 1`.

results.title: Wright's `F_ST = 1 / (1 + 4 N m)` (Wright 1931)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For demes of `N` diploids (`M = 2N` gene copies) and migration fraction `m = κ / (4N)`, so that `4 N m = κ` is held fixed, the equilibrium `F*` tends to `1 / (1 + κ)` as `N → ∞`.
